text:
Brock Nelson is 35, past 1,000 games, and Sports Illustrated just wrote about his latest milestone as another chapter for one of hockey's great families from Warroad. On the ice he's playing like a man who doesn't care about the number. He scored twice and added an assist against Anaheim on Thursday, and has 8 goals and 16 points in 23 games on almost 18 minutes a night.

That's a slower pace than last season's 33 goals, but the underlying game is strong. Colorado gets about 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, almost five points better than without him. His 8 goals have come on 5.9 expected, a little ahead of his chances. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 98th percentile among forwards at driving play last season, with the caveat that his teammates are excellent.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the reason he scores: he lives in front of the net, 96th percentile among forwards for chances from the slot. He's also been clutch by our wins-added numbers, 62nd in the league. We'd watch the power play, where 7 of his points have come.
